title: Well-Formed Continuation Expressions
purpose: Define the grammar, typing, and domain constraints for valid RT continuation expressions so reduction rules operate only on well-formed continuation structures.

canonical_claims.statement: Reduction is only lawful over well-formed continuation expressions.
Composition is only lawful when endpoints match and domain constraints are preserved.
Identity continuations are well-formed only over lawful RT conditions.
Domain errors block reduction and composition.
Well-formedness is structural and semantic, not merely syntactic.

formal_objects.name: Well-Formed Continuation Expression
formal_objects.definition: A continuation expression whose endpoints, composition structure, domain bindings, and governing constraints are valid.

well_formedness_rules.name: Endpoint Validity
well_formedness_rules.formal: WF(C(A,B)) only if A and B are lawful RT conditions.

well_formedness_rules.name: Composition Compatibility
well_formedness_rules.formal: WF(C(A,B) ∘ C(B,C)) only if cod(C(A,B)) = dom(C(B,C)).

well_formedness_rules.name: Identity Validity
well_formedness_rules.formal: WF(I(A)) iff A is a lawful RT condition.

well_formedness_rules.name: Reduction Validity
well_formedness_rules.formal: C ->red C' requires WF(C) and WF(C').

well_formedness_rules.name: Domain Guard
well_formedness_rules.formal: Meta-domain, affect/effect-domain, projection-domain, and continuation-domain symbols must not be substituted across domains without an explicit projection or binding rule.

validation_requirements: No occurrence treats WF(C) as primitive.

next_recommended_patch.title: Typed Continuation Domains
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Refine WF(C) by introducing explicit continuation-domain typing across meta, affect/effect, projection, observation, and operational-regime layers.
